recruitment_or_access: Founder's own or a consenting volunteer's recent amazon.co.jp, Rakuten and Yahoo order emails (redacted)
method: Inspect 3+ recent amazon.co.jp confirmation/shipping emails for item name, quantity, price, tracking number; repeat for Rakuten/Yahoo/a Shopify store
proceed_threshold: Item names + tracking numbers present in JP Amazon emails
stop_threshold: Amazon JP emails category-only and without tracking numbers
threshold_rationale: Amazon is the single largest merchant; without item identity the timeline is weak and exceptions cannot be matched
safety_boundary: Owner's own inbox only; redact before sharing; no third-party data
limitation: Snapshot; Amazon can change format again
decision_unlocked: Whether email-based ingestion is viable at all for the largest merchant

target_segment: Heavy multi-merchant households (>=3 merchants and >=4 parcels/month), incl. deliberately non-AI-enthusiast and low-pain profiles
recruitment_or_access: Recruit 20-30 via community posts/acquaintances-of-acquaintances with a screener; exclude friends who pitched the idea
method: 14-day consented diary: log each order, parcel, notification used, and any exception; participants forward order emails to a dedicated address OR log manually; founder runs a disclosed human 'concierge' that resolves exceptions on request (no account access; guidance and drafting only)
baseline: Participants' current tools (carrier LINE, merchant apps, Gmail)
metric: (a) share reporting >=1 material unresolved exception/month; (b) share sustaining forwarding to day 14; (c) minutes saved per exception; (d) share accepting a real paid offer
threshold_rationale: Subscription break-even needs ~17% paid conversion of actives (CLA-F07); exception service is the only untested pain; 14 days captures ~2 order cycles for heavy buyers
safety_boundary: Explicit consent; redaction; no logins/credentials; no purchases; delete data at end
limitation: Small self-selected sample; not representative; novelty effects
decision_unlocked: Proceed to a C04 prototype / pivot to B2B2C / stop consumer path

target_segment: EC merchants (D2C on Shopify, multi-channel sellers), 3PLs/WMS users, a card issuer or carrier partnership team
recruitment_or_access: Warm intros incl. founder's logistics network (no employer-confidential data)
method: 8-10 structured problem interviews on WISMO/returns/exception cost, current tools (Recustomer, AfterShip, OMS), and willingness to pilot a cross-channel exception service; ask for written pilot interest and indicative fee
metric: Partners giving written pilot interest with an indicative fee
proceed_threshold: >=2 written pilot interests at >= JPY 32/MAU/month (CLA-F09) or equivalent per-order fee
threshold_rationale: B2B2C needs a fee above ~JPY 32/MAU just to cover variable cost in base
safety_boundary: No fabricated commitments; no confidential data requests
decision_unlocked: Whether a payer exists outside consumers

target_segment: Same pool as E002 plus a broader screener list
method: A/B: (A) set up forwarding/selective forward, (B) Google OAuth read-only in testing mode (<=100 users, unverified-app screen disclosed)
metric: Permission grant rate; time to first parsed order
sample_plan: >=100 eligible visitors per arm if possible
safety_boundary: OAuth testing mode only; no restricted-scope production use before verification

method: Benchmark deterministic parsers + small-model extraction vs hand labels; measure order/package matching and latency vs carrier notifications
baseline: Hand-labelled ground truth; carrier LINE notification timestamps
metric: Field-level precision/recall; package-to-order match accuracy; critical errors
proceed_threshold: >=98% precision on order ID, merchant, tracking number; 0 cross-user leakage; >=95% package match
threshold_rationale: Wrong-order/wrong-user errors destroy trust; tolerable failures are 'unknown' states
safety_boundary: Redacted data; local processing where possible
decision_unlocked: Whether tracking can be reliable enough to show

method: For real upcoming purchases, offer delivered-price comparison with disclosed affiliate links (Rakuten/Yahoo/ASP); record handoff, completion and credited commission
metric: Handoff share of eligible orders; attributable share
safety_boundary: Disclose commissions (景表法); never buy for the user; no point-site interference
decision_unlocked: Whether C03 affiliate economics can work

method: Measure whether tracking users later use handoff without prompting
decision_unlocked: Whether to keep tracking and checkout in one company

method: Compute cash payable vs expected reward value (after caps, expiry, eligibility) across Amazon/Rakuten/Yahoo for each basket; time each optimisation
metric: Median net saving per basket (JPY and %) and minutes
proceed_threshold: Median saving >= JPY 300 per basket at <2 minutes user time
threshold_rationale: Below ~JPY 100 the value does not beat attention cost or point-site habits
safety_boundary: Points valued at realistic redemption, not face value
decision_unlocked: Whether points optimisation is a real wedge

recruitment_or_access: 1-2 hour consult with a Japanese privacy/consumer-law attorney
method: Scope: APPI Art. 28 for overseas LLM processing; telecom-business notification for an email-forwarding service; 景表法 disclosure for commission-funded recommendations; 特商法/電子消費者契約法 for handoff UX
metric: List of must-do obligations and costs
proceed_threshold: No blocking obligation for a forwarding/handoff MVP
stop_threshold: A blocking requirement (e.g., registration) with >3 months lead time
threshold_rationale: Compliance cost and lead time are business-model inputs
decision_unlocked: Go/no-go on handling external users' emails

method: Monthly check of re-open triggers: UCP/ACP/Shopify agentic checkout available to Japanese merchants; Visa/Mastercard agentic tokens generally available in Japan; amazon.co.jp agent policy; Alexa for Shopping in JP
threshold_rationale: C02 is a watch item; triggers define when it becomes testable
